#453 rework (ruling 359428): stopped before code. The smallest way needs a design choice.

Why: `RetryConfig` is the Turnkey SDK's type (`pub use turnkey_client::RetryConfig`), so a budget can't carry its own opt-out flag. The only hand the turnkey crate has is the budget's numbers, or new plumbing through `ClientFactory` and `turnkey::client`.

Options:
A (recommended). A rule in `read_delays`: a budget whose first sleep is under the first early read (100 ms) already reads sooner than the schedule, so it keeps its own backoff unchanged. This is one `if` and one doc line.
  - SIGNING_WAIT (50 ms x4): exactly as before 453. Four reads 50 ms apart, and the signing test is back to 1 + max_retries.
  - Default (500 ms) and signup's budget and SETUP_KEY_GRACE (2 s): on the shared schedule, unchanged from the current head.
  - Test budgets (turnkey behaviour and stamped_submission, 60 ms; account-service fakes, 10 ms): the turnkey tests go back to main's 10 ms and the diff shrinks. They then run on their own backoff as on main, and the schedule stays pinned by the unit tests.
  - Cost: it's implicit. Any future budget under 100 ms also opts out.
B. A named opt-out in the turnkey crate: an exported const budget (e.g. moving SIGNING_WAIT into turnkey), with `read_delays` skipping the early reads when the budget equals it. It's explicit, but it's matched on float-bearing struct equality, and a signing-service constant moves into turnkey.
C. A flag passed from signing-service through ClientFactory. The ruling excludes this as per-client machinery.

Awaiting a pick; A is ready to implement on your word.

deliveries.text:
Re the reviewer's P2 on 5460ad4dc (sockets pile up after a timed-out handshake): I confirmed it in sqlx-postgres 0.9.0 src/listener.rs:360-375. Drop for PgListener spawns a detached task that awaits "UNLISTEN *" and then return_to_pool, with no bound. When the timeout drops the handshake mid-LISTEN, that task waits forever on the stalled connection, and every retry adds one more.
Scope: it happens only when a server accepts and authenticates but then stops answering. Against a black-holed network the UNLISTEN write eventually errors on TCP retransmit (~15 min on Linux), so the pile tops out at about 15 min / (timeout + 1 s). Against a live but hung backend it has no bound.
I am not changing anything until the owner rules. The options I see:
 (a) Keep the timed-out handshake alive instead of dropping it: park it, and start no new attempt until it resolves. At most one socket is in flight, but reopens pause for as long as the server stays stalled (polling continues throughout).
 (b) Issue LISTEN on a plain pool connection under the timeout, and wrap it in PgListener only afterwards. This avoids the Drop task, but PoolConnection's own drop also returns asynchronously, and a notification arriving before PgListener attaches could be lost, which needs proof. I would not pick this without a test showing no ring is lost.
 (c) Accept it and document it as a limitation: bounded by TCP retransmit on a dead network, unbounded only against a server that is live but hung.
My recommendation is (a). It bounds the resource and keeps the poll backstop, which is what the ruling protected. The cost is no fresh attempt while one is stalled, and a fresh attempt against the same stalled server would stall too.

content.text:
A second problem has turned up in [468](https://github.com/infinex-xyz/boomerang/pull/468)'s LISTEN timeout. muho has confirmed it and is holding for a ruling.

**What happens:** when the timeout gives up on a stalled connection, the database library's cleanup keeps waiting on that connection in the background, and each retry leaves one more open socket. It only happens when the server accepts and authenticates the connection, then stops answering.
- If the network has died, the operating system closes the sockets after about 15 minutes, so they stop piling up.
- If the Postgres server is alive but hung, they pile up without limit. In that state the app's own database pool is hung too, so everything else is already broken.

**Options:**

| Option | What it does | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Accept and document (my pick) | Record it as a known limit in the README and the PR | Nothing new. Polling still works throughout |
| Keep the stalled attempt instead of dropping it (muho's pick) | Only one attempt in flight; no new attempt until it resolves | A little more state in the reconnect machinery. Reconnects pause while the server is hung |
| Listen on a plain connection first | Avoids the cleanup | Risks losing a notification; needs proof. Not recommended |

I pick accept and document because the case only arises when Postgres is already failing everything else, and you want less machinery, not more. The fix muho prefers is sound, but it adds a fourth state to handle a failure that has already taken the app down.

Which one?
